headline: OpenAI has been warning its staff that foreign spies may try to seduce, bribe or eavesdrop on them to steal AI secrets, the Wall Street Journal reports.
score_reason: Pool score 5 lowered by 1: the Wall Street Journal first reported it on 15 Oct 2026, before the window, from unnamed sources.
importance_line: OpenAI staff and other AI workers are affected first, then the firms whose research could be stolen, as the warnings follow a charged listening-device case, though the account rests on unnamed sources and OpenAI had not commented.
summary: The Wall Street Journal reports, citing unnamed sources and as relayed by the New York Post, that OpenAI trains its employees to watch for "honey pot" schemes, in which a foreign agent uses sex or bribes to get close to a target, and advises screen protectors in public, wiping whiteboards and avoiding logo clothing; the Post says Anthropic and Google have reportedly given similar warnings. The Post links the warnings to the recent US Justice Department charge against a Saudi engineer accused of hiding a listening device in an OpenAI executive conference room in San Francisco.
notes: Pool link (NDTV) blocked; read the New York Post, which relays the WSJ report of 15 Oct. WSJ original not read; its link is unconfirmed, so the New York Post page is given. Not carried in earlier editions.
